correctness.rationale: All-parameter binary construction partitions k petals by 0,1,2 marked counts; inequalities r0>=r2+1 in low regime and r2>=r0-1 or r0 in middle regimes guarantee sufficient petals. Each branch has exactly k nonempty connected blocks with common 0/1, 1/2, or 2/3 mark counts. Spanning-tree refinements preserve EF1 and attain each n through 2k+1. Lower binary witness forces hub value at least k-n+2>=3 against a nonhub bundle of at most one. Three exhaustive placement cases for the two weight-two vertices prove ternary obstruction for k>=4, with total-value contradiction for co-located vertices and hub-versus-unit-bundle contradiction otherwise. The finite verifier checked 18,048 binary size/valuation cases and exhaustive small negative instances, supporting but not replacing the symbolic argument.

value.rationale: The graph family is a canonical collection of triangles meeting at an articulation, providing a natural connected resource-division laboratory. Exact binary universal existence threshold and explicit ternary failure at that same sharp boundary identify a nontrivial valuation-granularity dependence beyond known general cutset and large-agent theorems. The construction covers an infinite family and every binary labeling, rather than recomputing a finite example.
